name: kernel_start
ownership: cluster-local (per-SM constant cache, per-warp issue); the grid axis only varies how many SMs start cold at once
why: Stall attribution (dev/design/stall-attribution.md, dev/status.md): on H100 the largest sign-consistent site gap is the code outside loops before the first anchor (hardware 5.15 % of a case's residency, engine 2.97 %, 272 of 500 cases below). Hardware-only: all imc_miss samples (2.67 % of residency) sit on ULDC instructions themselves, and 0.80 % of residency is no_instruction on the kernel's first instruction. The engine never holds a warp at a constant load: a constant load issues at once and only its consumers wait for the result. The existing constant_cache / constant_launch probes read the clock after every load, which cannot tell a hold at the load from a result latency, and they run one warp on one SM.
data_seen_before_freezing: Full-GPU site tables of $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/compare/ledger4 (both devices, 500 cases each) and the per-class instruction listing of the hardware samples (hw_where).

deepgemm_fp8_mgroup_contiguous_06 (H100, 1584 warps, 12 per SM, all first wave), cycles per warp in program order: first instruction `LDC R1, c[0x0][0x28]` no_instruction 302 (engine fetch 19, plus 131 of dispatch that the comparison leaves out); `ULDC.64 UR10, c[0x0][0x208]` imc_miss 409 at the ULDC (engine 0 there, 227 at its consumer 21 instructions later); `IMAD.WIDE` reading the result of `LDC.64 R4, c[0x0][0x440]` short_scoreboard 470 (engine reg:LDC:hit 12; the installed bank-0 vector rule is a flat 30); `ULDC UR4, c[0x0][0x144]` imc_miss 286 (engine 165 at the consumer). Hardware total 1467, engine 423.

Installed values this protocol is compared with: memory.constant_cache h100 miss 406.51 / hit 107.17 / same_line 37.0 / bank0_access_cycles 30.0 (vector path, measured at one warp, grid 1, launches 2..33); constant_launch v3 uniform path bank-0 first 288.5 (experimental) / second 68.0; launch.dispatch slot_free_to_entry 150.3 ns (297.6 cycles at 1.98 GHz).
These are suite observations. They motivate the cells; no value below is taken from them.

probe.binary: tools/microbench/kernel_start/probe/kernel_start.cu, built per device (sm_90a; sm_103a with -gencode arch=compute_103a,code=sm_103a).
probe.kernel: Every thread of every warp runs the same straight-line code; no thread-id dependent branch before the last clock. t0 = clock (the kernel's first statement); U constant loads x_k of U different 64 B lines (line k at byte offset 256 x k plus a warp-uniform, non-constant sub-line offset); F filler operations on a register chain that does not depend on any x_k; t1 = clock; y = x_0 + ... + x_(U-1) (the first use of every x_k); t2 = clock. Lane 0 of every warp stores t0, t1, t2 and y at out[(cta x W + warp) x 4 + j] after t2.
probe.paths: u: the index lives in uniform registers (plain C++ indexing with a warp-uniform kernel-parameter seed, as constlaunch_v3 k_uc0 / k_uc3) so the loads are ULDC (sm_90a) / LDCU (sm_103a). v: the address lives in a per-thread register (inline ld.param / ld.const as constlaunch_v3 CL_LD0 / CL_LD3 with independent addresses) so the loads are register-indexed LDC.
probe.banks: 0: a by-value kernel parameter struct of 4096 B. 3: a 4096 B __constant__ array written with cudaMemcpyToSymbol once before the first launch.
probe.cells: none (t0, t1 only; no load, no filler). For path in {u, v}: control n0.f4096 (U = 0, F = 4096); for bank in {0, 3}: n1.f0, n1.f4096, n4.f0, n4.f4096. 19 cells.
probe.shapes: g1.w1 (grid 1, 1 warp per CTA: the shape of the installed leaves), gS.w1, gS.w8, g4S.w8, with S = the device's SM count (configs/hardware/<device>). 4 shapes.
probe.launches: per (cell, shape) one process that launches the kernel 4 times; launch 0 (the first launch of that kernel in the process) and launch 2 are measured.
probe.sass_gate: per cell: between the first and the second clock read exactly U constant loads of the cell's path and bank (ULDC / LDCU with a UR index for u; LDC with an R index for v), every one to a different 64 B line, at least F filler instructions, and no instruction that reads a register written by one of the loads; between the second and the third clock read every load's destination is read. A cell failing the gate is recorded and not measured. The SASS of every measured cell is kept.

runner.clocks: ncu with the case reference conditions (python/cyclescope/capture/driver.py NCU_LAUNCH_METRICS, --cache-control all, --clock-control none, --replay-mode kernel); the stored t0 / t1 / t2 of launch 0 and launch 2 are read from the process output. Two independent runs per device: $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/microbench/kernel_start/<device>/run-{a,b}.
runner.stall_sampling: cyclescope reference --metrics --source-stalls, sampling interval 0, for the shapes gS.w8 and g4S.w8, launch 0 and (separate pass) launch 2, twice. The rows are added to suites/<arch>/microbench with set `kstart` so the same launches are traced and replayed with --stall-ledger.

derivation.clocks: per warp d1 = t1 - t0, d2 = t2 - t0; per (cell, shape, launch, run) the median over warps. filler = d1 of the path's n0.f4096 control. base = d1 of `none`. For a load cell: A = d1(n<U>.f4096) - filler (what the loads add before the filler chain ends); M = d2(n<U>.f0) - base (load to first use with nothing in between).
derivation.sampling: cycles per warp per (pc, class) as cyclescope.stall.hardware scales them. first = all classes but selected on the kernel's first instruction; at_load = on the constant-load pcs; at_use = on the pcs between the second and third clock read.
derivation.engine: the replay's stall ledger of the same launch: the same three sums by reason.

predictions_before_data.engine_today: A = 0 for every cell (a constant load never delays an instruction that does not read it); M = miss 406.5 (h100) for the first access of a bank-3 line and of a uniform-path bank-0 line, 30 for a vector-path bank-0 line; first = fetch only.
predictions_before_data.from_the_suite_observation: uniform path, cold: A is close to M (hold at the load) and at_load holds most of the wait as imc_miss on H100; vector path: A near 0 and the wait sits at_use; vector bank 0 at gS.w8 launch 0 has M well above 30; first is about 300 cycles on H100 at gS.w8.

outcomes_before_data.R1_hold_at_load: Per device, path and bank, for launch 0 (cold) and launch 2 (warm) separately, on shape gS.w8 with U = 1 and U = 4, both runs: the test needs filler >= 2 x M, else `undetermined`. hold when A >= 0.8 x M and (sampling) at_load >= 0.7 x (at_load + at_use); result_latency when A <= 0.2 x M and at_use >= 0.7 x (at_load + at_use); anything else `mixed` (reported, no rule). Engine rule declared now for a (path, cold / warm) that is `hold` on both banks it applies to: a constant load of that path whose line is missing or in flight (cold), respectively resident (warm), holds its warp at issue until the value is ready, with the latency the engine computes today; ledger reason `constant_hold`. The rule is installed per device from that device's outcome; no latency value changes.
outcomes_before_data.R2_first_access: Reported per path, bank, shape and launch: M, and for U = 4 the per-line slope (M(n4) - M(n1)) / 3. Finding (no install in version 1) when two runs agree within 10 % and a shape differs from g1.w1 launch 2 by more than 20 %: the condition under which a bank-0 line is resident at launch (the installed vector rule assumes always) goes to a version 2 with its engine rule declared before that data.
outcomes_before_data.R3_first_instruction: Reported per shape for the two n0.f4096 controls (`none` is too short for 2000 samples): first (hardware) against the replay's dispatch + fetch cycles per warp on the first instruction. When they agree within 15 % of the hardware value on gS.w8 and g4S.w8 in both runs: the comparison package counts the replay's dispatch cycles at a warp's first instruction as resident no_instruction (statistics only). Else finding for launch.dispatch / kernel.lifecycle.
outcomes_before_data.unusable: a cell failing the SASS gate, a (cell, shape) whose two runs differ by more than 10 % in M or A, or a stall-sampling row with fewer than 2000 samples is reported and decides nothing.

install: Only the R1 engine rule (a rule, not a value) and the R3 accounting change, each as its own commit; then the stall ledgers and the comparison of the full-GPU 500 x 2 are re-run. The rule is judged by the site table (code outside loops, constant-load pcs), not by the cycle error; the cycle error is reported next to it.
not_allowed: No latency value changed or added by version 1; no threshold, cell, shape or derivation change after data; no full-GPU case used to choose a value; no rule for a path or device whose own outcome is not `hold`.

addenda.when: after the SASS gate on h100, before any clock or sampling data
addenda.text: The four uniform-path cells with a single load (u.b0 / u.b3, n1.f0 / n1.f4096) fail the SASS gate: over the probe variants tried ptxas does not keep one isolated warp-uniform constant load as a ULDC between the first two clock reads (the tried forms and what was emitted are listed in $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/microbench/kernel_start/h100/build/gate_failures.md). 15 of 19 cells pass. Consequence for R1: the u path is decided on U = 4 alone (cells n4.f0 / n4.f4096), the v path on U = 1 and U = 4 as written. For U = 4 the quantities read the same way: A = d1(n4.f4096) - filler, M = d2(n4.f0) - base; whether the four holds add up or overlap is reported as A / M next to the per-load sampling at the four load pcs. Nothing else changes.

addenda.when: h100 run of version 1 (15 cells; clocks run-a / run-b; stall sampling 60 rows twice; engine replay build b3fb43de)
addenda.text: Data: $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/microbench/kernel_start/h100/raw.tsv (649560 warp rows), stall sampling and replay under $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/kernel_start/h100. Two things about the probe decide how far version 1 reaches. (1) The filler chain takes about 72000 cycles and varies by 2000-4000 cycles between runs and shapes, more than any M (200-4400): A as declared is noise (values from -1980 to +5067, the two runs disagreeing in sign); every load cell fails the 10 % run-agreement condition on A. (2) To keep the loads between the first two clock reads the probe has a MEMBAR.SC.CTA after them (in every kernel). The sampling shows the instruction after that MEMBAR waiting on the long scoreboard for outstanding vector loads (v.b3.n4.f0: 660 / 865 cycles per warp on the clock read after the MEMBAR), so no clock between loads and use can separate a hold from a result latency in this probe; this departs from the kernel as the protocol describes it and was found in the data. Outcome by the letter: R1 `hold` needs the clock condition, which is unusable -> no path is `hold`, no rule is installed from version 1. What the sampling alone shows (thresholds as declared, both passes, shapes g132.w8 and g528.w8, launches 0 and 2, all 8 uniform rows and all 16 vector rows): uniform path: the wait sits on the ULDC instructions themselves as imc_miss, one after the other (u.b0.n4.f0 g132.w8: 152 / 152 / 135 / 103 / 145 cycles per warp on the five ULDCs of the window, the kernel's pointer parameter included; share at the loads 0.93-0.99; the consumers wait 0-15); the sum of the sampled holds matches the clocks' M (758 / 789 sampled against 741 / 729). Vector path: nothing at the LDC (0-13 cycles); the wait is at the first reader or at the instruction after the MEMBAR (v.b3.n1.f0: 547 / 663 on the STG that reads the value). R2, reported (M per shape g1.w1 / g132.w1 / g132.w8 / g528.w8, run a / run b, launch 0): uniform bank 0, four lines plus the pointer parameter: 325/325, 384/380, 741/729, 736/721 (grows with warps per CTA, not with the grid; launch 2 the same within 10 %, both launches are cold under the reference cache control); uniform bank 3, four lines: 4112/4164, 3532/3432, 3636/3594, 4376/3753 (launch 2: 3303/3738, 2690/2514, 2926/2932, 3440/3041), i.e. 650-1000 per line against the installed miss 406.5; vector bank 3, one line: 1856/2168, 1571/1906, 1780/1659, 2254/1928 (launch 2: 965/973, 860/840, 882/930, 1090/1116). The vector bank-0 M (227 / 235 / 314 / 465) is not a clean single-load latency: its window also holds the seed's own bank-0 load and a uniform pointer load; the sampling puts 70-180 cycles per warp of short_scoreboard on the reader of the first vector bank-0 load of a kernel (installed flat value 30, measured at one warp on one SM with a clock after every load). R3: cycles per warp before the first instruction issues (no_instruction on the first pc): 220-300 on every row at both shapes and both launches (medians about 250), against the replay's dispatch + fetch of 150 at g132.w8 and 543 at g528.w8 -> they do not agree within 15 %: finding. Hardware is flat per warp across the grid; the replay's dispatch grows with the grid (serial dispatch, time a warp is not yet resident). Further findings outside the declared outcomes: the replay of the empty kernel takes 1694 cycles at g132.w8 against hardware 743 / 757 (2777 against 1057 / 1033 at g528.w8); the filler chain (shr / xor pairs) is 14 % slower in the replay (83.9 k against 73.6 k).

Same 15 of 19 cells pass the SASS gate on sm_103a (the uniform loads are LDCU). Clocks: $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/microbench/kernel_start/b300/raw.tsv (728280 warp rows, run-a / run-b). Departure from the runner as written: the ncu named by constant_launch/run_ncu_v3.sh (2025.1.0) fails to initialise on the B300 driver (LibraryNotLoaded); the runs use the image's ncu 2026.1.1, the one the full-GPU B300 reference was collected with. No stall-sampling rows: there is no blackwell microbench suite and the capture / reference routing needs runner code for one (not written). As on h100, A is noise against the 75000-90000-cycle filler and the probe's MEMBAR makes the clock test void; without sampling R1 and R3 say nothing on b300. R2, reported (M per shape g1.w1 / g148.w1 / g148.w8 / g592.w8, run a / run b, launch 0): uniform bank 0, four lines plus the pointer parameter: 378/367, 402/290, 366/314, 358/344 (no growth with warps per CTA, unlike h100; launch 2: 197/214, 309/482, 310/305, 220/293); uniform bank 3, four lines: 1911/2221, 1814/1879, 2012/2038, 1951/1828 (launch 2: 1177/1159, 976/780, 1008/1037, 1000/821); vector bank 3, one line: 2493/2189, 1692/1639, 1734/1673, 2098/1652 (launch 2: 1244/1221, 1036/1721, 1009/880, 998/1022); the vector bank-0 M (254/234, 232/232, 233/232, 355/357) has the same contamination as on h100. Run agreement is worse than on h100 (several cells differ by more than 10 %).
